introduction.title: No one knows much.
introduction.description: No one knows much. In life, we only see a corner of the world, and we see beyond it by watching what others say or do.

chapter-1.title: Baseline Linear-Quadratic-Gaussian Games
chapter-1.description: One player’s action changes what the others learn, their response feeds back into the state, and the first player must price it.

chapter-2.title: Delayed Public Signals and Asynchronous Learning
chapter-2.description: Public information often arrives after private learning has already occurred. Delay creates a disclosure window during which a private action can move what others infer.
chapter-2.card: Delay creates a disclosure window during which a private action can move what others infer.

chapter-3.title: Stationary Infinite-Horizon LQG
chapter-3.description: The calendar drops out and only ages remain, the age of the shock and the age of the belief about it.

chapter-4.title: The Information Wedge in a Stationary Kyle–Back Market
chapter-4.description: In a Kyle–Back market an order is at once a trade and a signal. It earns or loses money at execution, and it changes what the market maker and the other traders infer from order flow.

chapter-5.title: Local Strategic Information in Symmetric Network Economies
chapter-5.description: A regional credit market may contain only a few major lenders. A local labor market may be dominated by a few employers. Such players are atomistic globally but oligopolistic locally.
chapter-5.card: Players who are atomistic globally but oligopolistic locally: a few lenders, a few employers.

chapter-6.title: Monitored Deviations: Naive Distortions and Privy Responses
chapter-6.description: A strategic market maker requires a different equilibrium test. Its quote must be an admissible control, and changing the quote unilaterally must not improve its payoff.

chapter-7.title: The Information Wedge Across Environments
chapter-7.description: Every equilibrium in this dissertation is a set of kernels against the same primitive shocks. The chapters changed what players could see, and the coordinates never moved.

afterword.title: Afterword
afterword.description: My background was originally in cognitive neuroscience. It started from looking at optical illusions.

appendix-a.title: Additional Finite-Horizon Extensions
appendix-a.description: The obstruction to optimizing precision in the multi-player setting, and other finite-horizon extensions.
